$comment: Among the stars and beyond (src/ui/explore/neighbourhood-panel.ts): loaded with its chunk (I18n.extend). The scene’s labels and the navigator’s entry are in en.explore.json.
ui.universe.stars.title: Among the stars
ui.universe.stars.intro: Each star where its Hipparcos parallax puts it, as bright and in the colour it would look from here, and 2.4 million more from Tycho-2 as they look from near the Sun. Drag to look round, scroll toward the pointer, fly with W A S D, and double-click a star to fly to it.
ui.universe.stars.where: Here: {ly} light years ({pc} pc) from the Sun
ui.universe.stars.camera.label: How the camera moves
ui.universe.stars.camera.keys: W A S D fly, R and F rise and sink, Q and E roll, Shift is faster; the arrows turn; O orbits the star in view or lets it go; Esc stops a flight, then goes back to the solar system.
ui.universe.stars.camera.speed: Flying at {ly} light years a second, {c} times the speed of light
ui.universe.stars.light.title: Star light
ui.universe.stars.light.note: The eye under a dark sky reaches about magnitude 6.5, Tycho-2 about 11.5. How bright a star is drawn is a display mapping of its real magnitude, the same at any screen’s pixel density.
ui.universe.stars.light.count: Drawn: {placed} stars placed in space, {far} more as directions on the sky.
ui.universe.stars.figures: Constellation figures between their stars’ places
ui.universe.stars.planets: {count, plural, one {# known planet} other {# known planets}}
ui.universe.stars.planetsNote: From the NASA Exoplanet Archive. Values it calculated rather than measured are marked. Orbits are drawn face-on to the Sun, tilted by their inclination where it is measured; where each planet is on its orbit, and its size, are illustrative.
ui.universe.stars.planet.temperature: about {k} K if it absorbed all its light evenly
ui.universe.stars.search: Find a star (a name, or HIP or HR and a number)
ui.universe.stars.nearWithPlanets: {pc} pc away, {count, plural, one {# planet} other {# planets}}
ui.universe.stars.fromSunWithPlanets: {pc} pc from the Sun, {count, plural, one {# planet} other {# planets}}
ui.universe.stars.unplaced: its distance not known well enough to place it
ui.universe.stars.credit: Places: ESA’s Hipparcos (the 2007 new reduction, van Leeuwen; Alpha Centauri’s, Kervella et al. 2016); faint stars: Tycho-2 (Høg et al. 2000); names: the IAU’s; planets: the NASA Exoplanet Archive. The Milky Way’s glow is the density of Tycho-2’s faint stars, its brightness illustrative; the figures join the sky’s constellation lines. Black holes: the papers named with each; light bending computed, their gas illustrative. Beyond: the Milky Way a model (Reid et al. 2019; Bland-Hawthorn and Gerhard 2016); the Local Group, McConnachie (2012) and SIMBAD (CDS); galaxies, the Sloan Digital Sky Survey.
ui.universe.stars.whereFar: Here: {ly} light years ({pc}) from the Sun
ui.universe.stars.holeAway: a black hole {ly} light years away
ui.universe.stars.holes.title: Black holes
ui.universe.stars.holes.intro: Seven black holes, each where it is measured to be and of the mass measured. Close up, each is drawn by how its gravity bends the light from behind it.
ui.universe.stars.hole.massRange: {low} to {high}: two estimates from one spectrum, each uncertain by a factor of about three (drawn at {high})
ui.universe.stars.hole.redshift: Redshift {z}: its light left it {gyr} billion years ago
ui.universe.stars.hole.here: Here: {n} of its radii from it ({d})
ui.universe.stars.hole.ring: The Event Horizon Telescope measured a ring {uas} ± {e} microarcseconds across round it, just outside the shadow.
ui.universe.stars.hole.companion: A star orbits it: {kind}, once every {days} days.
ui.universe.stars.hole.model.thin-disc: A model: a black hole that does not spin, of the mass drawn; the bending of light round it is computed. Its disc of hot gas is illustrative (its temperatures, colours and size are not measured); the shift and brightening of the gas’s light by its motion and the hole’s pull are computed.
ui.universe.stars.hole.model.hot-ring: A model: a black hole that does not spin, of the mass drawn; the bending of light round it is computed. The thin hot gas round its shadow is illustrative, as the Event Horizon Telescope’s radio images show such a ring (not its colours); the shift of its light by its motion and the hole’s pull is computed.
ui.universe.stars.hole.model.dormant: A model: a black hole that does not spin, of the mass drawn; the bending of light round it is computed. It has no disc of gas: what is drawn is the sky behind it, bent.
ui.universe.stars.group.rest: neither: the Local Group itself, or near it
ui.universe.stars.beyond.title: Beyond the stars
ui.universe.stars.beyond.intro: Scroll out past the stars to the Milky Way, the galaxies around it and the web of galaxies a survey has mapped, or go to:
ui.universe.stars.beyond.view.web: the galaxies a survey has mapped
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.galaxy: The Milky Way here is a model, not a picture. Its arms are where the parallaxes of star-forming regions trace them (Reid et al. 2019), continued more faintly beyond; its disc and bar are at their measured sizes (Bland-Hawthorn and Gerhard 2016). Its stars are not individually known.
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.local-gro: The galaxies of the Local Group are where McConnachie’s catalogue (2012) puts them, each a glow of its own size and brightness. The four largest are discs of points at their measured sizes and tilts; which side of each is nearer is not known. The Milky Way is the model.
ui.universe.stars.beyond.scale.universe: Each point a galaxy the Sloan Digital Sky Survey measured ({count} drawn), placed by its redshift (Planck 2018’s cosmology). The survey covers part of the sky and takes fewer galaxies farther out: the outline is the survey’s, the filaments and voids the universe’s.
ui.universe.stars.hr.title: The stars by colour and brightness
ui.universe.stars.hr.label: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram: {count} stars by colour and brightness from 10 parsecs, the Sun circled{marked}.
ui.universe.stars.hr.caption: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram of {count} stars placed in space, each by its colour and its brightness from 10 parsecs (Hipparcos). Most lie along the main sequence, fusing hydrogen in their cores; the giants have left it and swollen; white dwarfs are cores left behind. The Sun is circled, the star in view ringed.
ui.universe.stars.hr.captionOff: A Hertzsprung–Russell diagram of {count} stars placed in space, each by its colour and its brightness from 10 parsecs (Hipparcos). {name} is not on it: its colour, or its distance, is not known well enough.
ui.universe.stars.lightV: Its light in V, the Sun’s as 1
ui.universe.stars.radiusEstimated: Radius, the Sun’s as 1 (estimated from its light and colour)
ui.universe.stars.plxFrom.companion: Its distance is its close companion’s ({hip}), measured better.
ui.universe.stars.plxFrom.kervella-2016-: Its distance is Kervella et al.’s (2016) for the pair, measured better than Hipparcos’s.
ui.universe.stars.luminosity: All its light, the Sun’s as 1
ui.universe.stars.archiveStar: Radius, mass and light as the NASA Exoplanet Archive gives them for a planet’s star.
